principles.text: Diversify income and take chips off the table; algorithms can change overnight and wipe out a single source.
Software has no product moat now. Distribution is the edge, so plug every launch into your own YouTube, X and newsletter.
Always be testing, and never trust a guru's tactic until you've validated it yourself on multiple sites.
When a test hits, drop everything and sprint at it with the whole team; if it doesn't, kill it or leave it on autopilot.
Post content every day and do more of what performs; consistency beats talent.

sampleQA.question: How should I launch a new SaaS product?

answer.text: Build from a pain you have yourself. Replace tools you already pay for with something better and cheaper, and people with the same problem will come.
Talk about the topic on YouTube for a long time first. LocalRank did $20K at launch, and 90% of that came from YouTube.
Validate cheaply: connect one Meta pixel across all your sites and spend about $30 on a retargeting campaign for each launch.
If it fits your audience, go all in. If it doesn't, kill it or leave it on autopilot.

sampleQA.question: When should I build links to a new site?

answer.text: On a new site, stay conservative: one or two branded links a month to the homepage, no exact-match anchors.
Buy paid links and niche edits only after a page is already in the top 10.
Judge vendors by rankings and traffic over months, not DR. Many give an early bump, then tank.
Use a different link mix on each site so one update can't hit your whole portfolio.

sampleQA.question: How do I land my first local SEO clients?

answer.text: Build rank and rent sites (one service plus one city) so you own a lead-gen asset that earns while you pitch.
Start with pay-per-lead or a monthly rental. Save percentage-of-revenue deals for business owners who have proven they can close.
Follow the progression: parasite SEO for your first dollar, then rank and rent, then client work, then partnerships.
Niche down. Become the physio marketing guy in one city and take one client per neighborhood.
